notes: app/page.js is a 'use client' component, so it CANNOT export `metadata` or `generateMetadata` (Next.js forbids metadata exports from client components). All SEO/meta content for '/' therefore comes only from app/layout.js's root `metadata` export, which Next merges into every route including Home.

app/layout.js metadata only sets `title` and `description`. There is no openGraph, twitter, icons, keywords, canonical, or robots block anywhere in the app. No app/favicon.ico, app/icon.*, or app/opengraph-image.* file exists, so Next.js emits no custom favicon/OG image for this app — flagged so the schema author knows these fields are currently entirely absent, not merely empty.

components/Home/HomeSection/WorkLookBanner.jsx exists on disk (video hero banner: 'This is what the' / 'work looks like.', video/work-look-banner.mp4) but is NOT imported by components/Home/HomePage.jsx and is not referenced anywhere else in the repo (verified via grep). It is therefore dead/unused code and is EXCLUDED from this inventory per the Home-page-only scope. If it is meant to render on Home, it should be added back to HomePage.jsx and re-audited.

components/Blog/BlogCard.jsx is not imported by components/Home/HomeSection/BlogSection.jsx (BlogSection builds its own <article> markup inline instead of reusing BlogCard). BlogCard.jsx is therefore out of scope for this audit.

components/Blog/data/blogData.js is imported by BlogSection.jsx and IS in scope, but only 4 of its 7 fields per entry render on the Home page (title, date, category, image/alt via the 3-up preview grid). The `excerpt`, `comments`, and `content` (long-form HTML) fields exist in the data file but are not rendered anywhere on '/' — they belong to the /blog and /blog/[slug] routes, which are explicitly out of scope. Not included as Home-page fields for that reason.

blogData.js currently has exactly 3 entries and BlogSection does `blogs.slice(0, 3)`, so all 3 blog posts in the data file appear on Home today. If a 4th post is added to the data file it will NOT appear on Home (slice cap), which the CMS schema/population script should account for.
CustomCursor.jsx (rendered by app/App.js, part of the shared shell) renders only a decorative cursor-follower <div> with no text/media content — excluded as pure structure/interaction, not content.

Loader.jsx exists at the project root but is NOT imported/rendered anywhere (app/App.js implements its own inline loader instead, with brand text captured under globals.loader). Loader.jsx is dead code and out of scope.

app/App.js (rendered by app/layout.js around <Header/>{children}<Footer/>) contains an intro loader with a hardcoded brand string, captured under globals.loader since it appears on every page load of '/' as part of the shared shell.
HeroSection.jsx declares an unused `gridCells` array (Array.from({length:60})) that is never referenced in the returned JSX — dead code, not rendered, excluded as content.

Several literal background-image URLs live in components/Home/HomeCss.css rather than in inline `style` attributes: `.three-pillars-stack-card { background-image: url("/images/three-pillars-banner.jpg") }` (HomeCss.css:395) backing all 3 ThreePillarsSection cards, and `.creative-future-col:nth-child(n) .creative-future-card::after { background-image: url("/images/future-iconN.png") }` (HomeCss.css:722,726,730,734) backing the 4 CreativeFutureSection stat cards. These are genuine rendered media (not decorative CSS-only patterns) so they ARE captured below as media fields on their respective sections, with a note that today they are only editable by changing the CSS file, not via any component prop — a CMS-driven version would need to convert these to inline styles or next/image elements.

Two other CSS background-image declarations were found and deliberately EXCLUDED as pure design (repeating grid-line patterns, not depicting any subject): components/Home/HomeCss.css:29-32 (`.hero-section-area::before`, a linear-gradient grid overlay) and public/styles/style.css:74-78 (`.hero-section::before`, an unrelated/unused grid overlay for a `.hero-section` class that does not appear in any Home component's className list).

BrandsSection.jsx builds each of its 14 tile background images from a template: `linear-gradient(135deg, ${t.tone}cc, ${t.tone}66), url(https://picsum.photos/seed/${t.seed}/800/1000)` — i.e. every 'brand' tile is currently a random Lorem-Picsum placeholder photo keyed by a `seed` string, NOT a real product/campaign photo, and NOT run through next/image. `t.tone` is a hex color used only for the gradient overlay and is DESIGN, excluded from content; `t.seed` is captured below because it is the only content-relevant driver of which placeholder image renders. The `https://picsum.photos` host is not declared in next.config.js `images.remotePatterns` (which only lists images.unsplash.com and images.squarespace-cdn.com) — this is fine today only because the image is applied via raw CSS background, not next/image, and no remotePatterns entry in next.config.js is actually consumed anywhere in the Home page scope as audited.

Two strings use JSX HTML entities in source rather than plain unicode: HeroSection.jsx:63 `doesn't` and TheShifSection.jsx:47 `isn't`. Both are recorded below using their RENDERED value (a plain straight apostrophe, U+0027) since that is what reaches the DOM/CMS field; the entity form is preserved here in this note for traceability.

OutlinedBandSection.jsx repeats the literal phrase "ORGANIC - PAID - AI - " 15 times via `.repeat(15)` to fill a marquee track; the field below stores the base phrase plus the repeat count rather than the full ~330-character concatenated string, since the repeat count is itself a code-level layout detail a CMS field would not need to store verbatim.

Every anchor currently pointing to href="#" (Header primary/submenu items except Blog, the Header CTA, all Footer links except the mailto, all Three Pillars list-item links, the Talk Discovery CTA) is a PLACEHOLDER destination with no real target page. Flagged per-field below with `"notes"` but called out here in aggregate: a CMS `href` field for these should not be assumed production-ready.

No raw inline <svg>...</svg> markup was found anywhere in the audited scope (app/page.js, app/layout.js, app/App.js, HomePage.jsx, all 10 rendered HomeSection components, Header.jsx, Footer.jsx, CustomCursor.jsx) — verified via grep for '<svg'. All icon-like assets in scope are either Font Awesome webfont classes (Footer social icons) or raster/SVG *files* referenced by path (logo-img.svg, logo-img2.svg) rather than inlined markup, so the ./inventory-assets folder created for this audit contains no extracted files.
Font Awesome CDN stylesheet and 3 Google Fonts <link> tags in app/layout.js (lines 16-21) are asset/typography loading, not content strings, and are excluded per the DOES-NOT-COUNT design rule.

Header.jsx's mobile hamburger toggle button renders 3 empty <span> bars with no text/aria-label at all (Header.jsx:109-113) — flagged as a real accessibility gap (missing aria-label on the toggle button) but there is no string literal to capture as content.
